title: Request Exchange Ledger for Dedicated Onboarding
creator: Sofia Patel
description: We will build a Request Exchange Ledger (REL): a canonical, auditable record that standardizes reservation intake, negotiation rounds, provisional throughput escrow, and final approval handoff for Dedicated capacity onboarding. REL is designed to reduce back-and-forth between account teams and customers, provide deterministic capacity commitments for the fleet planner, and produce traceable artifacts for billing, compliance, and rollback. The ledger model captures: 1) request metadata (expected qps, peaktokens, seqLen profile, model family), 2) automated sizing suggestions and cost estimates, 3) negotiation steps (proposal / counter-proposal), 4) provisional allocations and probation windows (probation escrow tokens), 5) approver decisions and SLA bindings, and 6) lifecycle events (commit, amend, decommit, deprovision). This ticket scopes the PM and UX requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout sequence, and integration contract for engineering teams (runtime, fleet, billing, and security).
acceptance_criteria: 1) REL API exists to create/update/append negotiation events and returns stable request IDs. 2) Every new Dedicated reservation goes through REL in the UI and API; at least 90% of sample onboarding requests receive an automated sizing suggestion. 3) Provisional allocations (escrow) are represented and consumable by the fleet allocator (ENG-5621) during probation windows. 4) Audit trail captured for every decision (who, when, notes) and surfaced on the Console request detail page. 5) Billing shows estimated vs committed throughput for signed reservations during the trial period. 6) Security review completed and KMS key reference attached to ledger entries for PII-sensitive notes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): API-only REL and web console stub for internal concierge; integrate with fleet allocator mock; sample: 10 customer onboarding exercises (2 weeks). Phase 2 (beta): surface REL in self-serve reservation flow, automated sizing enabled, probation escrow visible, connect billing estimates (1 month). Phase 3 (GA): full integration with Dedicated onramp, canary with 5 customers, SLA signatures and enforcement, telemetry for SLO/latency impact. Post-GA: add delegated approvals and quota trades. Each phase gated on metrics (automation rate, approval latency, incorrect sizing <10%).
open_questions: What fields are required in the canonical request schema to enable reliable sizing across model families?
How long should probation escrow last by default (7/14/30 days)?
Should cancellations during probation trigger partial refunds or credits?
What RBAC model do we use for delegated approvers (account admins vs finance)?
Do we allow automated acceptance rules for low-risk customers?
